name: Nativism in United States politics
summary: American nativism favors the native-born (historically Anglo-Protestant) majority over immigrants and treats newcomers as a threat to national culture, loyalty and wages. Its recurring program is immigration restriction, long delays before citizenship, preference for natives in office, assimilation and reserving benefits for citizens. It is a cluster of movements, from the Know Nothings to the 1920s quota era to modern restrictionism, rather than a full philosophy, so it says little about economics or other issues.
scope: Mainstream of US nativism as documented in Wikipedia's overview: the 1850s Know Nothing / American Party (1856 platform), the 1882-1924 exclusion and quota era, and the modern restrictionist strand including Huntington's cultural argument. It excludes European nativism and treats issues outside immigration, culture, citizenship and welfare as low-confidence inferences.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nativism has no healthcare doctrine; adherents split between welfare-protective labor voices and anti-state conservatives, and the Know Nothings were mixed on state spending.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Unions that backed exclusion did so to protect wages, but modern nativists are divided on wage mandates, so no settled position.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Know Nothing branches mixed hostility to elites with support for regulation, and later nativists include both free-market and protectionist wings.

public-ownership.rationale: Nothing in the sources links nativism to public ownership; the 1856 platform is silent and modern American nativists lean toward private enterprise.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Know Nothing populism was hostile to wealthy politicians, but nativism has no tax doctrine and modern adherents lean pro-tax-cut.

unions-good.rationale: Labor unions were among the strongest backers of immigration exclusion, yet nativism as a whole is not a labor creed and modern adherents are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not addressed by nativist sources; the 1856 platform respects vested rights but makes no claim about property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Some Know Nothing state branches backed industry regulation while others did not; there is no common nativist line.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nativists stress that immigrants should not draw on public benefits, and Boston relief costs fed 1850s fears, but cutting welfare in general is not a defining demand.

worker-ownership.rationale: Nothing in nativist sources supports collective ownership; inferred from its focus on nation rather than class.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Modern nativists back border enforcement and security measures framed against foreign threats, but no source states a surveillance position.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Know Nothings were forerunners of temperance and strict liquor laws, and modern nativists lean law-and-order, so adherents likely oppose legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nativists mostly treat restrictions on speech about immigrants as censorship; inferred, not stated in sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Nativists have favored both party organization and strongman figures such as Trump, but the doctrine does not demand a strong leader.

state-harmful.rationale: Nativism wants a state that excludes, enforces borders and defines membership, so it is the opposite of anti-statism; the 1856 platform insists on enforcing law and Union.

limit-guns.rationale: Modern American nativism sits in the gun-friendly right; the 19th-century sources say nothing on arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: Enforcement-heavy immigration policy (walls, troop deployments, deportation) implies more enforcement capacity, though not stated as a general demand.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Moral-conservative and Protestant roots of the Know Nothings point against it; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The 1856 platform defended states' reserved rights, yet nativists demand national restriction, and the two pull in opposite directions.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from law-and-order tilt and the exclusion of criminals from entry; sources do not address prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Nativists link national character to Protestant and later Christian norms, but family structure is not a defining claim.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Modern nativists mostly sit on the cultural right; the issue is anachronistic for earlier phases.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the Protestant-Christian and culturally conservative alignment of modern nativists; not stated in sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Know Nothings wanted Protestant Bible reading in public schools and defined American identity partly by Protestantism, while the platform also opposed church-state union.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Nativism has centered on preserving a racial and cultural majority, and the 1924 law rested on 'preserving the racial composition' of the country.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the cultural-conservative position; no source addresses it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The central nativist claim is that immigrants threaten American culture, language, religion and values, as Huntington's Anglo-Protestant argument also states.

gradual-change.rationale: Nativists conservatively want to preserve inherited culture, but the Know Nothings and later movements were also radical in their demands.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Quotas, exclusion laws and reduced levels are the movement's signature policy demand from the Chinese Exclusion Act through 1924 to the modern reduction movement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: 'Americans must rule America' and the demand to exclude those owing allegiance to foreign powers imply hostility to outside authority.

free-trade.rationale: Protectionism appears in Trump-era nativism and in labor support for exclusion, but sources tie it only loosely to nativism.

nation-first.rationale: Putting native-born citizens' interests first is the defining nativist principle, and the 1856 slogan was 'Americans must rule America'.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Modern nativists tend toward restraint and anti-refugee politics; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Nativists demand exclusion, quotas and enforcement, so open borders are the direct opposite of the program.

limit-growth.rationale: Some restrictionists have used environmental arguments for population limits, but this is not a common nativist position.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Modern American nativists lean skeptical of drastic climate policy; not a doctrinal matter.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no nativist doctrine on energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nativist movements generally sought legal and electoral restriction, and the platform stresses upholding the Constitution, though riots occurred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Nativists present themselves as defenders of ordinary native-born citizens against elites, though the Dillingham Commission lent expert cover to restriction.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred as strongly contrary to the American-patriot and property-respecting tradition; no source addresses it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Nothing in nativism supports worker or public ownership; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No nativist doctrine on land taxation.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No nativist doctrine on inheritance tax.

basic-income.rationale: Nativists oppose giving public money to those they see as outsiders and favor reserving benefits for citizens; unconditional income is unlikely to be backed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Wage protection against immigrant labor and Trump-era protectionism link nativism to tariffs, but the link is not central in the sources.

state-directs-investment.rationale: No nativist doctrine; modern adherents divide between free-market and economic-nationalist wings.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No source ties nativism to distributism; the 1856 platform respects vested property rights.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Nativism is not corporatist; inferred from its absence in sources.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nativists organized through competitive party politics, as the American Party did, and the platform defended constitutional republican government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nativism arose around republican American identity and distrust of foreign princes; the platform bars officeholders owing allegiance to a foreign prince.

democracy-best.rationale: Nativists claim to defend democracy for native citizens but want to narrow who may vote and hold office, so support is qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed by sources; some modern nativists favor referenda on immigration, but it is not doctrinal.

right-to-secede.rationale: The platform stresses perpetuating the Federal Union, so nativists generally oppose secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: 'Americans must rule America' reserves power for the native-born as a group, not for people with an innate fitness to rule; the sources offer no theory of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nativist movements produced riots and violence, such as Louisville 1855, yet mainstream adherents condemn it; adherents are split.

separate-church-state.rationale: The platform opposed church-state union and test oaths, yet Know Nothings wanted Protestant Bible reading in schools; the tension leaves it split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The platform opposed union of church and state, so nativists mostly reject scripture-based law even while valuing Protestant culture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Contrary to nativism's emphasis on a strong national state; inferred.

military-superiority.rationale: Nation-first attitudes imply support but sources are silent.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nativism holds that the nation belongs to its established native group; the 1924 act aimed at preserving 'the ideal of U.S. homogeneity', and Madison Grant spoke of racial dilution.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nativism sees the main conflict as native versus foreign, not class; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not a nativist concern; inferred from the right-leaning character of most phases.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: 'Native' in nativism refers to European settlers' descendants, not Indigenous peoples, and adherents do not back Indigenous land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nation-first outlook is hostile to foreign claims; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nativists favor the nation-state and reject outside allegiance, though Anglo-Protestant identity has pan-Western echoes.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No source addresses the moral status of self-interest; nation-first claims are collective, not individual.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not a nativist claim; the platform stressed constitutional rights.

limit-population.rationale: Restrictionists who want lower immigration sometimes call for population stabilization, but domestic population limits are not defining.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred; nativism champions American national development.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Nativist sources say nothing about technological change, and their preservationist cultural stance cuts against speeding it up, leaving no clear lean.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from cultural conservatism; no source.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred distrust of unaccountable systems.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No nativist source addresses encryption; enforcement-minded adherents might oppose it while liberty-minded ones favor it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nativism holds that earlier American cultural homogeneity is being eroded, a restorative framing, but it also pursues new restrictions.

direct-action.rationale: Mostly pursued through party politics and law, though street violence occurred; split but leaning against.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nativism offers no doctrine on whether methods must mirror aims; adherents range from electoral organizers to rioters.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Nativists reserve public benefits for citizens, not distribution by need; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nativism frames conflict as native versus immigrant rather than worker versus owner; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed in nativist sources; some modern adherents hold it, most do not.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; Know Nothings backed temperance laws restricting private conduct, but other nativists differ.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nativism ranks native-born citizens above others as a group, so rights are not purely individual; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nativism treats voting and citizenship as precious and restricts them to natives; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on running government like a business, though modern adherents sometimes admire business-style leaders.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not a nativist concept; inferred from the right-leaning framing.

media-academia-power.rationale: Modern nativist populists often attack media and academia, but the doctrine does not require it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: 1920s nativism leaned on race science, including Madison Grant's racial-dilution argument, though modern nativists like Huntington frame their case as cultural. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

organic-representation.rationale: Not a nativist idea; inferred from party-political organization.

total-state.rationale: Nativism does not call for total state direction; the platform sought limited government under the Constitution.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nativist rhetoric about decline and defending national identity points toward renewal, but this is not a stated program.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nativist sources focus on who is inside the nation rather than on expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The 1856 platform bars officeholders who owe allegiance to a foreign power and rests rule on constitutional supremacy.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred; nativists generally do not take a relativist view.

universal-morality.rationale: Nativism claims a particular Anglo-Protestant heritage rather than universal moral truths, and sources do not address the question.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not a nativist issue; American nativism was historically also antisemitic in places, while modern adherents split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship by ancestry abroad is not a nativist demand, although the platform gave native rights to children of American parents abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not applicable; nativists promote English as the existing national language.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not addressed; the platform called for economy in spending.

economic-freedom.rationale: Nativist sources never link political and economic freedom; the movement's economic wing is split between free-market and protectionist positions.

rule-by-example.rationale: The platform stresses constitutional law; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nativists believe a nation should govern itself without foreign influence, though the principle is not a stated nativist doctrine.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nativism's religious dimension (Protestant identity) makes it unlikely to rest on reason alone; inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Reserving public benefits for citizens, as in the public charge rule and exclusion of paupers from landing, is a standard nativist demand.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Nativists emphasize self-reliance and keeping dependents out; conditionality is common but not defining.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nativism is cross-class but does not preach collaboration doctrine.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nativists place great weight on preserving inherited American culture and institutions.

workers-nation.rationale: Labor backing of exclusion shows nationally organized workers' interests, but this is not a doctrine.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nativists backed segregation of Chinese and Japanese in places, but the doctrine is about immigrants and not a general segregation code; adherents split.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Modern American nativist politics aligns with the energy-expansion right; not doctrinal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Demands that newcomers give up foreign culture and language run from Know Nothings to the English-only push and Huntington's 'dream in English'.

elite-replacement.rationale: Modern nativists increasingly voice replacement ideas, but this is not a historical or consensus nativist doctrine and many adherents reject it.

national-mission.rationale: Know Nothings and later nativists stressed protecting America rather than spreading its government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist leanings; not addressed.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: 1920s nativism overlapped with the eugenics movement, but the issue is not central today.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Not addressed; nativism wants a state strong on borders and citizenship.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Racial-dilution concerns of the 1920s imply it, but no source states a position on intermarriage.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Nativism ranks native-born over immigrants in rights and office, and the 1924 act valued preserving racial composition, which conflicts with equal rights for all.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nativism defines 'native' as settler descendants and rejects framing the US as a colonial project; inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Nativists demand a single American law and loyalty; sources do not discuss religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The platform guarantees no interference with religious faith or worship.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Know Nothing state governments required Protestant Bible reading in public schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The platform's republican constitutional framing implies it, though consent is limited to a narrowed citizenry.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade surpluses are mercantilist, and only Trump-era economic nationalism touches the idea; nativism as a whole takes no stand.

population-transfer.rationale: Mass deportation proposals recur in modern nativism, but pressure on minorities to leave is not standard doctrine; split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nativists accept state coercion at the border; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Race-science nativists saw struggle between peoples as real, but sources give no general stand on competition as the engine of progress.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican-theory claim is not addressed in nativist sources, and its adherents would not read it as bearing on immigration.

separated-powers.rationale: The platform insists on upholding the Constitution and states' reserved rights.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Nativism prioritizes natives, not the poor as a class; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Unions backed immigration exclusion, but nativist sources say nothing about strike law, and modern adherents lean pro-employer without a doctrine.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed, though restrictionists cite immigration's effects on wages.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nativists hold that immigrant diversity threatens national unity, and Huntington warns of 'two peoples, two cultures, and two languages'.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not a nativist idea; the platform wants native-born officeholders chosen by election.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Alien and Sedition Acts show nativist willingness, yet many adherents invoke constitutional supremacy; split.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Long waits before citizenship are a signature demand: 14 years in 1798 and 21 years in the 1856 platform.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No nativist source addresses pay for legislators, though populist hostility to elites could tilt some adherents toward it.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The American Party was an organized secret order with oaths, yet sources do not state a doctrine of binding party decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: 'Americans must rule America' and the ban on officeholders owing allegiance to foreign powers imply rejection of pooled sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The platform stresses Constitution and Union without taking a position on who commands forces; US practice already gives the president that role.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Know Nothings were Protestant and distrusted the hierarchical Catholic church; inferred.

clerical-rule.rationale: The platform opposed union of church and state, and the Know Nothings feared clerical control of voters.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nativists demand undivided loyalty; the 1856 platform excludes those with foreign allegiance and WWI nativists persecuted perceived disloyalty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; some adherents back moral censorship.

recall-officials.rationale: Nativist sources never raise recall elections, so no position can be drawn.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Early nativism was isolationist-leaning but modern adherents split; no stated position.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nativist sources are silent on militias versus professional armies, and modern adherents back both gun rights and military funding.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not a common nativist claim, although anti-immigrant politics often cast cities as immigrant centers.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist-leaning modern nativists often say so, but doctrine does not require it.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nativism treats Anglo-Protestant culture as the American core and foreign cultures as threats; Huntington says the national creed came from that culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from law-and-order orientation; not stated.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from cultural conservatism; anachronistic for early phases.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Know Nothings pushed Protestant Bible reading in schools, but sources do not mention evolution, so adherents are split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Know Nothings were moral reformers, but no nativist doctrine on pornography exists.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Nativists favor limiting citizenship for children of immigrants (Trump criticized birthright citizenship), but the 1856 platform instead gave native rights to Americans' children abroad; no settled view.

minority-language-support.rationale: Nativists fought German- and Spanish-language use and backed English-only measures.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Nativists opposed Catholic claims on public institutions, such as schools; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nativists demand conformity to American norms; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign debt relief is outside nativist concerns, although a nation-first view would hesitate to forgive debts owed to Americans.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: This postcolonial claim has no counterpart in American nativism, and sources take no position.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Nativists defend the existing US Constitution, so rewriting it is not on their agenda, yet no source states a view.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nativists put their own citizens first and oppose duties to outsiders, including refugee resettlement.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The US already has its own deterrent and nativist sources do not discuss it, so the question does not separate adherents.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Sources do not address how the president should be chosen; nativists work within the Electoral College system.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is absent from nativist sources, and populist adherents are split on the Federal Reserve.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: This is a territorial-dispute question outside US nativism, whose sources do not discuss it.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Nativist sources are silent on the philosophy of property; the platform only promises no interference with vested rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate internal to the Marxist left that American nativism never engaged.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred; modern American nativists tend to resist environmental regulation.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between isolationist and hawkish wings.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nativist sources never discuss annexation law, so no position can be drawn.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Know Nothings sought to limit Catholic church power and property but also defended religious freedom; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nativists defended the Union, so likely accept force, but sources do not say.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The US president is both head of state and a partisan leader, and nativist sources do not call for separating the roles.

region-keeps-system.rationale: This one-country-two-systems idea is foreign to US nativism, which wants uniform national law and loyalty.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Contrary to republican American nativism, which barred allegiance to foreign princes.

flat-income-tax.rationale: No nativist source covers income tax design, and adherents hold varied views.

character-from-environment.rationale: Racial-stock arguments imply innate factors, though culture-based nativists such as Huntington emphasize upbringing; leaning against.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside nativist sources, so there is no stated position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The platform insists on enforcing constitutional law and supremacy of the Constitution.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The platform backs the Constitution but does not argue for a mix of few and many, so no position is stated.

leader-cult.rationale: Trump-era adherents embrace a leader focus but the doctrine does not require it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is unrelated to the nativist program, and the sources do not address it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Inferred; the platform protects vested rights.

refugee-return.rationale: Nativists oppose refugee admission and resettlement, so a right of return with descendants is hostile to them.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not a US nativist position; inferred from nation-first focus on existing borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The platform guarantees no interference with religious faith and opposes test oaths.

women-must-cover.rationale: Modern nativists have targeted Muslim practices, but US nativists do not generally want to mandate dress codes for women.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from opposition to pooled sovereignty.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nativists defend the American nation-state; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Nativists demand assimilation into a single national culture rather than autonomous minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: This question about persecuted minorities choosing emigration has no clear nativist stance, since nativists oppose immigration but not minority rights abroad.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nativism stresses culture and race over economic base; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Nativist sources do not address antitrust, and adherents are split between pro-business and anti-elite populist positions.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts were not a nativist issue; Tea Party strands opposed them but the doctrine does not.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Modern nativists criticize courts blocking immigration policy, while the platform backed constitutional supremacy; split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; economic nationalism is present in modern strands only.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Nativism has no stated view on trade agreement standards; adherents are skeptical of agreements generally but divided on this.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Nativism works within law and elections; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed, though the platform opposed foreign titles of allegiance.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nativists want schools to teach American identity and Anglo-Protestant roots, as Huntington's argument implies.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: US nativism looks inward at immigrants rather than ruling other societies, and the sources give no position.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nativists have pressed schools to Americanize immigrant children, including through Bible reading and English-language instruction.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from opposition to race-conscious remedies; not stated in sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary reform is outside nativist sources, so no position can be drawn.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nativist sources have no theory of capitalist crisis, so the question has no stated answer.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The US had no predecessor empire in the sense of this statement, and nativism does not address it.

delink-world-market.rationale: Economic nationalists in modern nativism favor protection but not delinking, and sources give no position.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred; nativism holds that American workers are harmed by immigrant competition.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nativists want to discriminate in immigration law but do not take a stand on private association.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The platform supports constitutional supremacy but mentions no bill of rights; split.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial-era boundary treaties are outside US nativism, and no source addresses them.

elective-rulers.rationale: Platform rests on elected republican government.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The platform insists on enforcing law and constitutional supremacy but never addresses resistance to rulers, so adherents are split.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Not applicable to a presidential system; no position.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is outside the nativist program, and sources take no position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is outside the nativist program, and sources take no position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Nativist sources say nothing about duties of the privileged, though Know Nothing reforms included some social-welfare measures.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nativism is a politically mobilized movement, such as the party organization behind the 1856 platform.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Populist-leaning nativists, notably in the Tea Party and Trump era, blame elites for immigration policy, and Know Nothings were hostile to wealthy politicians, but it is not a defining claim.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine with no counterpart in American nativism, so no position can be drawn from the sources.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Nativist sources never address price controls, and modern adherents split between market and interventionist wings.

native-born-offices.rationale: Plank 3 of the 1856 platform says Americans must rule America and prefers the native-born for state, federal and municipal office.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: nativism is a politics of national culture and loyalty, not a Marxist-style critique of media; it fears foreign influence rather than a pacifying mass culture.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: nativists blame immigrants and elites for national decline and do not theorise consent-making institutions; the claim belongs to a leftist framework.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: restrictionism concerns wages and culture at home; nativists generally treat poor countries' poverty as their own affair, not as extraction by the rich.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: nativism has no stance on communist party autonomy; its only related concern, foreign allegiance (s2), does not decide the question.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the insistence that America look to its own people first and the Huntington-style wariness of outside entanglement; never a stated plank.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: nativism is inward-looking and defensive about borders; it is not documented as an irredentist program.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The 'natives' nativism defends are the settler-descended, historically Anglo-Protestant majority, so leadership by them over later arrivals is the opposite of this claim.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: the strand spans the 1850s to the present and never addressed constitutional anti-fascism; adherents are split, so the answer is neutral.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the strand's hostility to radicals and foreign ideologies in the early 20th century and its modern anti-communism; not a documented plank.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Nativism was a northern and southern movement (the Know Nothings split over slavery, s5), so adherents do not share one view of the war's cause.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: a politics of defending inherited national culture and its symbols leans toward keeping them; not stated in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on gender and education; adherents are split or indifferent.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on domestic violence services; adherents are split or indifferent.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Huntington's cultural argument (s4) that American institutions rest on Anglo-Protestant culture and do not transplant automatically.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: the Know Nothings and later restrictionists worked through parties and legislation and not through the military, in line with American civilian control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on domestic labour; adherents are split or indifferent.

filial-duty.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on family duties; adherents are not united on it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Know Nothings wanted offices reserved for the native-born by election, so selection by examination is not part of the program; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to foreign influence; modern restrictionists favour barring foreign takeovers of strategic firms, though it is not a core issue.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on divorce; adherents are divided between social conservatives and others.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not an issue the movement addressed; adherents have no settled position.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: No doctrine on pensions; adherents are split between protecting Social Security for natives and privatising it.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: the movement defended private property and homesteads for citizens, so community tenure of land conflicts with it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the republican tradition many nativists claimed; not a topic of nativism itself.

single-official-language.rationale: Nativists press assimilation into Anglo-American culture and insist on English as the common language, a recurring modern restrictionist goal.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's suspicion of foreigners and the 1856 platform's stress on native Americans ruling America; land ownership is not a stated plank.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Nativists oppose affirmative-action style remedies and treat discrimination as intentional unequal treatment; inferred from the movement's stance.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: No stated position on consumerism; nativists are split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Nativism is mainly domestic and has little to say about foreign insurgents; inferred from its generally isolationist tendency.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nativists were historically isolationist and focused on the home country; inferred, with no stated position.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: nativism says little on economics; some nativists blame elites, but the sources give no settled position on lobbying and campaign money.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the nativist fear of foreign loyalty and influence (1856 platform bars those owing allegiance to a foreign power), which supports limiting foreign-funded bodies.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Inferred: modern restrictionists prefer raising native births to immigration to sustain population, but earlier nativism did not address it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred from reserving benefits and rights for citizens and natives, which would extend to local limits on who may buy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: nativism seeks to reserve benefits for citizens and is not associated with state employer-of-last-resort schemes.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nativism is about immigration, not foreign policy; no source records a position on democratic peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred: the movement stresses allegiance, law-and-order and loyal citizenship, so a general denial of a duty to obey is alien to it.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the 'America first' isolationist strand of restrictionism, though the movement itself did not frame foreign policy.

industrial-unions.rationale: Nativism has no position on union structure; its interest in labour is wages and competition from immigrants.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Know Nothings treated Catholics and immigrants as agents of a foreign power (the Pope) plotting against the republic, though modern restrictionists use cultural rather than conspiratorial language.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred: nativists defend traditional family and civic order, so abolishing legal marriage is unlikely to be backed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; nativists have no consistent view on government transparency.

local-production.rationale: Nativism does not address where goods are produced; economic nationalism is a possible but unsourced link.

informal-organisation.rationale: Inferred: the movement organised through parties and lodges such as the Know Nothing American Party, not informal small groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Inferred from the 'Americans must rule America' stance (1856 platform), which favours national authority over foreign or international power.

religious-nation.rationale: Historic nativism was anti-Catholic and Anglo-Protestant, but modern restrictionism (Huntington) defines identity by culture and creed broadly, so adherents are split on religion as the test.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from nativist insistence on American sovereignty and independence; not an addressed topic.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on regional revenue; adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on property; economic views vary across its strands.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred from Red Scare era nativism that linked foreign radicals to subversion; strands differ.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No nativist doctrine on service delivery; adherents split between welfare-protective and anti-state views.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred from the Protestant Christian identity of the Know Nothings and modern Anglo-Protestant cultural arguments.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nativism says little about capitalism; adherents range from labour protectionists to business conservatives.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the traditional cultural orientation of most nativist movements; not addressed directly.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from cultural conservatism and the preference for private, family arrangements; not addressed directly.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Nativists backed English-language assimilation and an English Language Amendment; purging loanwords is an extension.

treaties-binding.rationale: Nativists have generally sought to curtail the claims of non-assimilated groups; inferred, not stated.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred from nativist emphasis on a single national culture and national unity over separate communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the assimilationist aim of binding regions to the dominant culture; not documented as a plank.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Nativism has no economic doctrine and its strands span many positions on capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nativists claim priority for native-born Americans and the founding stock over later arrivals, a related but not identical idea.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Inferred: mainstream nativism does not rest on Holocaust denial, though fringe strands overlap.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Nativists have no distinct doctrine on this; adherents range from socially conservative to indifferent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: nativists wanted to restrict immigrants, not suppress opposition generally, though some exclusion-era measures were repressive.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Know Nothings were anti-Catholic but defended constitutional religious freedom for Protestants, so civil punishment is not their stated aim.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: nativists have been split between isolationism and expansionism on empire.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: it is hostile to foreign religious movements and has no sympathy for jihad.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: it opposes religious-law rule and Islamic politics.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred: nativists claim to speak for the native people but have no stated view on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: it rejects identity-based overlapping oppression as a framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative character of modern restrictionism; not a core nativist topic.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from cultural and religious conservatism; not addressed in the sources.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: nativists see the main divide as native versus foreign, and favour a distinct national culture.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: it is not a Marxist concept and nativism favours cultural over class analysis.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from restrictionist concern that Muslim immigrants clash with American culture, as in Huntington's cultural argument.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Know Nothings were Protestant, but their platform stressed the Constitution and not divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: no stated doctrine; anti-Catholic strands objected to Catholic influence in schools.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: not addressed in the sources and no nativist doctrine on employment law.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address economic systems, and nativists were split on state spending.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: it is nationalist and favours a strong national defence.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred: nativism tends to protect native workers and not wealth gaps, though not a stated doctrine.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from the isolationist tendency in the Know Nothing and 1924 restriction era.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nativists venerated republican government and the Know Nothings opposed aristocratic and foreign rule, but they never addressed inheritance of office; inferred from American republicanism.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: No nativist position on the structure of credit; adherents ranged from populist anti-bank views to pro-business conservatism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Modern restrictionists often favour national sovereignty over foreign institutions, but nativism has no doctrine on lender conditions; adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: The Know Nothings sought long naturalization delays for immigrants, not a wealth test, and modern nativists do not back one; adherents are split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nativism has no ecological or gender doctrine, and its conservative adherents generally reject the radical eco-feminist claim; inferred.

reification.rationale: Inferred from a conservative, nationalist outlook that does not frame markets as concealing social relations; nativism has no economic theory.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Nativists generally defend existing press and property arrangements, and the Know Nothings and later restrictionists focus on foreign influence, not on class ownership of media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform defended the Constitution and established law, and nativists framed their program as rule by republican law against foreign influence.

racial-franchise.rationale: The 1856 American Party platform reserved offices for the native-born and the 1924 Act ranked immigrants by national origin, but these are birth and origin limits, not a franchise limited to one race; modern restrictionists reject racial limits.

online-participation.rationale: Nativism predates the internet and has no position on online participation; adherents are split.

open-government-data.rationale: No documented nativist position on open records, though it appeals to populist distrust of elites; adherents are split.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Historic nativism was anti-Catholic and Protestant-centred, and some strands favoured protecting the community's religious identity, but laws against interfaith marriage were not a central demand; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Anti-Catholic nativism included informal economic exclusion of Catholics, though a boycott of shops is inferred rather than a documented platform plank.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: nativists worked through parties, legislatures and statutes (Know Nothing platform, 1924 act) rather than lot-chosen assemblies, and distrusted open deliberation by a mixed public; not discussed in the sources.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from historical nativism’s defence of an inherited Anglo-Protestant identity and its hostility to Catholic and other imported religions, which favours preserving established doctrine over reinterpretation; not stated directly.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Nativism is about immigrants and national culture rather than wealth; adherents range from labour-protective to business-friendly, so it is neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from nativism's association with traditional, Protestant social conservatism; the issue was not raised before the modern era.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from nativism's historic Protestant identity, which treated religion as part of national character; state atheism would contradict it.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nativists demanded stricter enforcement of order and borders, so abolishing police and prisons is inferred as strongly rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from its preference for rule by the native-born majority over shared power with distinct communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on charity; it sought to reserve benefits for citizens, and adherents split between church or local aid and public programs.

term-limits.rationale: Not a nativist issue; the Know Nothings and modern restrictionists took no stated position.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from its preference for citizenship-bound, conventional representative institutions and its distrust of newcomers' political influence.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed by nativism; its concerns are immigration, culture and citizenship.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from nativism's Protestant and conservative religious traditionalism, in which clergy offices were male.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family model of the eras in which nativism was strongest; the issue was not raised.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Nativists want long delays before naturalisation and political rights reserved for citizens, so voting by non-citizens is opposed.

rent-control.rationale: Nativism has no housing doctrine and adherents split between labour-protective and anti-regulation voices.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the strand's conservative defence of existing property and institutions; not an issue it addressed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Nativist fraternal orders drilled and paraded, but uniformed state youth training is not a stated plank; inferred opposition to state-run youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nativism never addressed nuclear basing, and adherents' views on it follow their wider conservatism.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; nativists mix isolationist suspicion of foreign entanglement with support for a strong military.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from nativist resistance to recasting national history around the wrongs done to other groups; not stated.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Nativist movements had a producerist, labour-protective strand that valued native workers' wages, though the sources do not state this principle.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Protestant culture of the movement and its emphasis on defending home and nation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Huntington's argument holds that American identity is rooted in an Anglo-Protestant culture continuous from the founding settlers.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook of nativist movements; the question is not one they addressed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook; nativism has no feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nativists honoured war dead but not as martyrs or saints in a religious sense; adherents are split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Know Nothings cast Catholicism as a threat, but nativism as a whole frames politics as culture and citizenship, not spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nativism wants immigrants to assimilate into the American nation, not to treat the country as a centre for a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about restricting immigration and assimilating newcomers within an existing state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the traditional Protestant outlook of historic nativism; not addressed.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook; not addressed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the program of preferring natives for office and jobs and fear of immigrants' effect on wages; the sources do not state it about economic ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from the strand's focus on a single national territory; not addressed.

independent-unions.rationale: Nativist movements were about immigration and never took a distinct line on union independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nativism had no theory of socialism or class power; it is silent on this question.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nativists took no distinct position on who should own local utilities; none is documented.

second-chamber.rationale: Nativism did not address legislative structure; inferred as indifferent.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the Know Nothing and restrictionist mainstream accepted private enterprise and proposed no communal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Confederal municipalism is outside nativism's concerns; no position is documented.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Know Nothing concern for native-born workers' jobs and wages, which fits a family-supporting wage.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is outside nativism's concerns.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is anachronistic and unrelated to nativism's program.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: restrictionists want immigrants' status and finances tracked and enforced, which sits badly with untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is anachronistic for most of nativism and unrelated to its program.

person-over-state.rationale: Nativism subordinated immigrants' claims to the native community but took no general line on the person and the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the Know Nothings' Protestant Christian outlook, such as Bible reading in schools.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nativism did not address the structure of regional self-government.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology is anachronistic and unrelated to nativism's program.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from nativist hostility to crowded, immigrant-filled cities as threats to native culture.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The 1924 Act aimed at racial homogeneity, and nativists defended the native majority's interests, though the focus was ancestry and origin rather than race in general.

racial-pride.rationale: Nativists treated Anglo-Protestant ancestry as the national core and valued it; Huntington's argument defends that heritage.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nativists were split between isolationism and nationalist assertiveness; no settled position on war.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Defines the nation by native birth and Anglo-Protestant culture, and treats religion as a divide, not a unifier across borders; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Know Nothings feared separate Catholic political loyalty and demanded single assimilation, so separate electorates are opposed; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nativists fear foreign subversion and loyalty, but not typically partition plots; no stated position.

free-public-college.rationale: No doctrine on tuition; adherents split between state spending for citizens and fiscal conservatism.

pollution-taxes.rationale: No environmental doctrine; modern restrictionists lean conservative and against new taxes; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Conservation for later generations fits a heritage-minded outlook, though not a doctrine; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Emphasis on national security and border defense makes arms reduction unattractive; inferred.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Know Nothing-era isolationism suggests openness to avoiding foreign entanglements, but no stated stance on secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: No stated position; protectionist instincts conflict with free-market conservatism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Nativism has no gun-control doctrine; adherents split between order-minded restrictionists and armed-citizen conservatives.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the movement's stress on loyalty and duty to the American nation, which sits badly with refusing orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Nativists feared immigrants undercutting wages but left no doctrine on bargaining, and adherents split on unions.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Never addressed; inferred only that views on income supplements are split between welfare-protective and anti-state strands.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between fiscal conservatives and those who accept state spending for natives.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the restrictionist 'Americans first' outlook, which opposes obligations to reshape the world economy for others.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The American Party sought to win office and use the existing state to restrict immigration and naturalisation, not to replace it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's wish for uniform national rules on citizenship and culture; it has no stance on economic pluralism.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Never addressed; inferred that adherents are indifferent or split between conservationist and extractive views.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nativists treat the nation and its core culture as something to be preserved against dilution, as in Huntington's argument about American identity. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the preference for reserving public benefits for native citizens and a restrictionist, fiscally cautious stance.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the view that regional and ethnic grievances are secondary to a single national identity.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the tradition of ranking immigrant groups as less assimilable, which rejects a universal shared human nature as a basis for equal standing.

public-service-media.rationale: Never addressed; adherents split between suspicion of media establishments and support for public institutions.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Historic nativism was Anglo-Protestant and anti-Catholic, treating other faiths as alien rather than as expressions of one truth; inferred from that religious framing.

farm-price-support.rationale: Nativism has no farm policy, and its adherents split between agrarian populists and market conservatives.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the nativist emphasis on national security and sovereignty; the movement never addressed nuclear arms.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Know Nothings built a cross-class native-born coalition and the American Party was a broad party, so a separate workers' party sits outside the tradition; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Modern restrictionists cite practices of recent immigrants as grounds for requiring assimilation to national norms; inferred from that assimilationism.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nativism has no stated position; 19th-century nativists and modern restrictionists differ on gender and property law.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Nativism stresses one national language, but the question of regional names for a language is not one it addresses.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on pollution; adherents split between regulatory and anti-state conservatives.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nativists want office reserved for native-born citizens elected through ordinary republican institutions, leaving no formal place for traditional leaders; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Nativism is silent on environmental trade-offs; some restrictionists link immigration to environmental pressure, others oppose regulation.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the modern restrictionist alignment with law-and-order politics; not a stated nativist plank.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Assimilation to the national culture and English is central, and Huntington's argument stresses a shared language; the audit's own missing statement backs English-only schooling.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Nativists and unions overlapped in wanting to restrict immigrant labor, but the movement had no settled stance on union membership.

voter-id.rationale: The 1856 platform wanted long residency before naturalization and offices for natives, and modern restrictionists stress citizenship as the basis of voting. None of the cited sources takes up this question, so the answer is an inference.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Nativism was historically Anglo-Protestant and anti-Catholic, so it favored a dominant Protestant culture; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Nativists used elections but wanted to limit who could join the electorate; the strand has no settled view on this definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Protestant moral and cultural conservatism.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the movement's concerns; inferred as neutral.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The movement wants benefits reserved for citizens and has no cash-transfer program; inferred as disagree.

women-suffrage.rationale: Nativists were split: some backed votes for native-born women against immigrant men, others held to traditional roles.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Protestant cultural identity; it did not frame religion as oppressive to women.

race-social-construct.rationale: The 1924 quotas rested on ancestry-based assumptions about national origins, so a scientific-basis view is inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred from its cultural conservatism.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Nativism has no property doctrine; the Know Nothings were mixed on land policy, so this is left neutral.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Nativist stress on national sovereignty and distrust of foreign influence suggests opposing courts above the nation; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Historical nativism was Protestant-identified, but modern restrictionism is mostly secular; adherents are split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Nativism did not address Indigenous or national self-government; no basis for an answer.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anti-foreign and anti-communist stance in the restriction era suggests no support for such a state; inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: Nativists wanted native-born citizens to rule through ordinary elections and the 1856 platform stresses popular rule; inferred.

national-church-status.rationale: The Know Nothings were anti-Catholic and Protestant-leaning but backed no established church; modern strands differ.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Nativism demands assimilation to a single national culture, which rules out ethnic territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: No stated position; nativism concerns immigration and not territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by a US immigration-focused movement; no basis for inference.

simple-living.rationale: No doctrine on consumption or self-sufficiency; left neutral.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Nativism restricts newcomers to protect the existing majority, but it centres on settler-descended natives, not Indigenous peoples; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: No stated position; adherents are split on gender and military service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred: nativism sees America as the natives' heritage, but sources discuss culture and citizenship more than land.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the movement was a constitutional party and not an advocate of summary killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Asian exclusion of the quota era and Huntington's cultural-defence argument.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred: nativism asks immigrants to give up foreign allegiance, so state support for kin abroad runs against it.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: nativism has no economic doctrine of common ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: No position documented; nativism is silent on self-ownership.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Nativism has no documented tax policy beyond reserving benefits for citizens.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Nativists want benefits reserved for citizens, not tested by income, so no clear answer is documented.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the Know Nothings were themselves a political party working through elections.

no-business-privileges.rationale: No documented position on business favouritism.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: Know Nothings opposed Catholic bloc voting and church influence in politics, as the platform's church-state planks show.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: No documented position; nativism is not a view about technology.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; no stance can be inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the movement's national-first, anti-foreign preference.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Nativism has no doctrine on how wealth is distributed, so adherents are mixed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The question is outside nativism's concerns and adherents are mixed on finance and taxes.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from modern restrictionist arguments, such as Huntington's, that culture and policy matter more than racism; contested within the strand.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the Know Nothings' legalism and stress on order and the rule of law; the question is not nativist doctrine.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the stress on wages and jobs for natives; the question is outside nativism's concerns.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the American Party's 'Americans must rule America' stance and wariness of foreign influence.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Nativism has no theory of value, though it frames immigrants as undercutting wages.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Nativism is patriotic and presents immigrants as a threat to native wages, but it is not a workers' politics as such.

material-over-identity.rationale: Cultural identity and national culture are the core of nativism, as in Huntington's argument, and come before economic interests.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from nativism's hostility to foreign ideologies; party-led communism is foreign to the movement.

missingStatements.text: Public offices should be reserved for native-born citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: Plank 3 of the 1856 platform says Americans must rule America and prefers the native-born for state, federal and municipal office.

missingStatements.text: Immigration should be limited by national-origin quotas that favor the existing population's ancestry.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1924 act set quotas by nationality on the 1890 census to preserve the country's racial composition.

missingStatements.text: People who owe allegiance to a foreign power should be barred from political office.
missingStatements.rationale: Plank 5 of the 1856 platform bars officeholders who owe allegiance to a foreign prince, potentate or power, aimed at Catholics in practice.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow historical plank of the 1856 platform aimed at Catholics; too specific to pose to other ideologies, and nativist suspicion of foreign loyalty is partly covered by native-born-offices and reduce-immigration.

missingStatements.text: Public schools should teach in English only.
missingStatements.rationale: Nativists opposed German and Spanish use in schools and backed an English Language Amendment.

notes: Strands differ: the Know Nothings were chiefly anti-Catholic, the 1920s restrictionists racial and eugenic, and modern adherents cultural or economic. Most non-immigration answers are low-confidence inferences, so inclusion may be thin.
